subject: Request: traffic zoning narrative & evidence for Acme Private deployment
messages:
From: Daniel Turner <daniel.turner@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Traffic zoning & isolation evidence for Private deployment

Hi Priya,

Acme is preparing for our vendor security review next week. The security team asked for a short narrative and evidence package that explains how traffic is zoned between tenant workloads and the control plane for Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem pattern). Specifically we need:  
- A short architecture narrative describing where tenant inference traffic traverses (ingress e.g., LB -> routing layer -> GPU pools) and the controls that enforce tenant isolation
- A network diagram (layered: ingress, routing, compute, control plane, egress) with callouts for where ACLs / VNets / VLANs apply
- A segmentation matrix (what flows are allowed between zones, ports/protocols, justification)
- ACL excerpts or example policies that cover egress restrictions and cross-tenant communications

Can you provide the narrative + attachments (PDF/png/csv) by EOD Monday PST? Also please indicate where audit logs for inference requests are retained and the retention period.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Turner
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp

---

(Please CC anyone on your side who typically handles Private deployment evidence)

Subject: Re: Traffic zoning & isolation evidence for Private deployment

Daniel — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (network/security lead) and Laura (solutions/ops) who will contribute artifacts.

Attached: traffic_zone_narrative_v1.pdf, segmentation_matrix_v1.csv, network_diagram_v1.png

Quick summary from the narrative (high level):
- Ingress & routing: Customer traffic enters via the customer-managed load balancer (for Private) or an ingress gateway in the VPC. In both modes requests are TLS-terminated at the ingress layer and then routed to a per-customer routing plane that maps to dedicated or logically-isolated GPU pools.
- Tenant isolation model: Each customer is placed into a dedicated "tenant zone" implemented as a combination of VPC subnet isolation + overlay tenant tagging on the routing plane. For Dedicated deployments we offer reserved GPU pools (hardware isolation or pinned instances) plus VLAN-backed isolation where required. For Private (VPC) we rely on subnet separation, strict security group rules, and customer-managed egress controls.
- Control plane separation: The control plane runs in a private management VPC and communicates with compute over authenticated service endpoints (mTLS). No customer application traffic traverses the control plane; only orchestration and health-check traffic is permitted via scoped service accounts.
- Egress & external services: Egress is restricted by default; outbound flows to third-party services require an allowlist entry that is logged. NAT gateways or managed egress proxies are used for centralized monitoring.
- Audit & telemetry: Inference access logs, request IDs, and model selection metadata are exported to the customer's chosen logging endpoint (managed object store or SIEM) and are also retained in Redwood for a configurable window. See attachments for retention defaults.

Key artifacts in the attachments:
- network_diagram_v1.png: layered diagram with labeled zones (Ingress, Routing Plane, GPU Pools, Control Plane, Egress Boundary) and arrows showing request flow and control plane channels.
- segmentation_matrix_v1.csv: explicit allowed flows between zones, port ranges, and justification (used for SIG/CAIQ answers).
- traffic_zone_narrative_v1.pdf: a 2-page narrative with bulletized controls and references to SOC 2 controls and KMS boundaries.

If you want a redline or a diagram with Acme-specific VPC names, we can produce a tailored diagram — happy to do that next.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Daniel / Priya — adding a short technical annex that callers typically request; attaching an ACL snippet for the egress policy. See egress_policy_acl_snippet.txt.

Technical annex (summary):
- Packet flow (inference request):
  1) Client -> Customer LB (TLS)
  2) LB -> Ingress gateway (TLS termination) with SNI routing -> routing plane (tenant-tagged)
  3) Routing plane performs policy check (ACLs + tenant tag) -> selects model-serving group (dedicated GPU pool or shared pool with tenant isolation)
  4) Model serving node handles KV cache and state; KV caches are namespace-scoped to tenant and are stored on encrypted persistent volumes.
  5) Response flows back the same path; telemetry (request-id, model-version, latency) is emitted to the logging pipeline.

- Controls and enforcement points:
  - mTLS between ingress, routing plane, and control plane.
  - Per-tenant routing tags + network policy at the edge of the compute plane.
  - Host-level firewalling to prevent lateral tenant-to-tenant flows; kernel-level seccomp and process isolation for serving containers.
  - Egress proxies enforce allowlist + header enrichment for auditing.

- Ports/protocols (examples):
  - Ingress TLS: 443/TCP
  - Routing plane gRPC: 8070/TCP
  - Internal orchestration APIs: 9443/TCP (mTLS)
  - Metrics/exporter: 9100/TCP (metrics only, not public)

- Audit logs & retention:
  - Real-time logs: routed to customer's logging endpoint (S3-compatible or syslog) with a default 90-day retention for managed retention.
  - Long-term export: customers can configure continuous export to their long-term archive; Redwood retains metadata and sampling copies for 365 days by default for investigation purposes (configurable under enterprise agreements).

Attachment stub: egress_policy_acl_snippet.txt (text, excerpt showing example deny-by-default rules and an allowlist entry for a SaaS connector).

If you'd like, we can produce the same annex with explicit iptables/nftables or cloud-provider security group snippets tailored to Acme's VPC names.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network & Security Lead, Redwood Inference

To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Traffic zoning & isolation evidence for Private deployment

Thanks Priya and Karthik — this looks good and addresses the bulk of our audit checklist. We'll review the attachments with the rest of the security team. Two quick follow-ups:  
1) Can you confirm the default retention windows in writing (you mentioned 90/365 days) and whether those are configurable per customer from the Console (or if we need a support contract change)?
2) For Dedicated GPU pools, can you confirm whether hardware pinning (physical isolation) is available as an option in our region?

If you can reply to those two items it will close out our network/isolation section. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Daniel
